code: # Create folders to store the input data dir.create("biodiversity", showWarnings = FALSE) dir.create("other_layers", showWarnings = FALSE)  # Get the paths to biodiversity rasters included in the package files_biod <- zonation5rdata_list("biodiversity", full.names = TRUE)  # Copy the biodiversity rasters to the local biodiversity folder file.copy(files_biod, "biodiversity", overwrite = TRUE)  # Get the paths to the additional layers included in the package files_other <- zonation5rdata_list("other_layers", full.names = TRUE)  # Copy these rasters to the local other_layers folder file.copy(files_other, "other_layers", overwrite = TRUE)

title: Working with variants in ZonationR
text: begin baseline prioritization using default settings.
code: # Run baseline variant in folder 01_baseline dir.create("01_baseline", showWarnings = FALSE) withr::with_dir("01_baseline", {   feature_list(spp_file_dir = "../biodiversity")   settings_file(feature_list_file = "feature_list.txt")   command_file(zonation_path = "C:/Program Files (x86)/Zonation5")   run_command_file(".") })

title: Working with variants in ZonationR
text: variant, change marginal loss rule Core-Area Zonation (CAZMAX). CAZMAX aims always cover high-occurrence locations features, even comes cost lower average coverage.
code: # Create the folder dir.create("02_cazmax", showWarnings = FALSE)  withr::with_dir("02_cazmax", {   feature_list(spp_file_dir = "../biodiversity")   settings_file(feature_list_file = "feature_list.txt")   command_file(zonation_path      = "C:/Program Files (x86)/Zonation5",                marginal_loss_mode = "CAZMAX" # We edit the marginal loss rule here   )   run_command_file(".") })

title: Working with variants in ZonationR
text: can assign unique weights features (e.g., species) increase priority areas features occur. allows emphasizing key species biodiversity features prioritization. purpose, use weight argument feature_list() function. ensure weights applied analysis, w flag must also included command_file() call. complete reference available analysis flags requirements ZonationR, please see vignette Analysis flags ZonationR.
code: # Create the folder dir.create("03_cazmax_w", showWarnings = FALSE)  # List files from the folder spp_files <- list.files("biodiversity", pattern = "\\.tif$", full.names = TRUE)  # Create a weight vector: default weight = 1 for all species weights <- rep(1, length(spp_files))  # Set higher weights for selected key species # For example, species 3, 7, and 10 are more important weights[c(3, 7, 10)] <- 5.0  # Run the prioritization withr::with_dir("03_cazmax_w", {   feature_list(spp_file_dir = "../biodiversity",                weight = weights) # setting weights   settings_file(feature_list_file = "feature_list.txt")   command_file(zonation_path = "C:/Program Files (x86)/Zonation5",                marginal_loss_mode = "CAZMAX",                flags = "w" # Flag w (use weights)   )   run_command_file(".") })

title: Working with variants in ZonationR

code: # Create a local copy of the example baseline folder src <- zonation5rdata_path("01_baseline")  # Copy the whole directory, preserving the structure file.copy(src, ".", recursive = TRUE, overwrite = TRUE)  # Define a variable for the baseline folder baseline_folder <- "01_baseline"

title: Exploring Zonation outputs
text: One main outputs Zonation priority rank map, shows conservation priority cell across landscape. Higher numbers indicate areas important conservation, lower numbers indicate areas lower priority. rank value tells cell compares others terms conservation priority. please note scale relative, absolute. example, cell ranked 0.8 twice valuable one ranked 0.4. priority map considered together outputs, like performance curves, fully understand spatial distribution conservation value, potential trade-offs, conservation effectiveness. can use priority_map() function visualize ranking values across landscape:  addition visualizing continuous priority values, can also adjust map make important areas stand clearly. classify argument priority_map() allows choosing whether display map continuous divided classes. classify = TRUE, map divided discrete classes, can define custom breaks labels make easier see areas higher lower priority.  visualization functions ZonationR return ggplot2 objects, means users can customize plots using ggplot2 ecosystem. example, can apply different color palette map:
code: p1 <- priority_map(baseline_folder)  print(p1) breaks <- c(0, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 1) labels <- c("very low", "low", "medium", "very high") p2 <- priority_map(baseline_folder, classify = TRUE,                    breaks = breaks, labels = labels) print(p2) p2 <- p2 + scale_fill_viridis_d() + labs(fill = "rank") print(p2)

title: Exploring Zonation outputs
text: performance curves describe much feature’s distribution covered protected grid cells following priority rank order. summary_curves() function helpful understanding overall performance solution. allows us explore key metrics : mean - average performance across species max - performance best-performing species min - performance worst-performing species  can also visualize additional metrics summary curves file using separate panels (facets). facet argument set TRUE plotting metrics different units value ranges.  Besides looking overall performance summary_curves(), one also interested feature represented across priority ranking, can explored using feature_curves() function:  priority_map(), functions summary_curves() feature_curves() return ggplot2 objects, allowing customization plots. example, can add vertical line highlight top 10% (rank = 0.9) priority cells.  vertical line 0.9 represents top 10% priority areas. Intersection curves shows proportion feature representation within areas. mentioned earlier, priority rank maps performance curves interpreted together. example, use priority_map() function plot classified map showing top 10% priority areas, alongside corresponding feature curves.  combining classified map feature curves side side, can see areas top-priority well species represented within areas (.e., curves intersecting red dashed line), providing integrated view spatial priorities species coverage.
code: p3 <- summary_curves(baseline_folder, metrics = c("mean", "max", "min")) +   ggtitle("Summary Curves") +   theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))  print(p3) p4 <- summary_curves(baseline_folder,                      metrics = c("remaining_area", "mean"),                      facet = TRUE) print(p4) p5 <- feature_curves(baseline_folder) +   ggtitle("Feature curves") +   theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))  print(p5) p5 <- p5 + geom_vline(xintercept = 0.9, linetype = "dashed", color = "red")  print(p5) # Define the threshold for the top 10% priority cells threshold <- 0.90  # Define breaks and labels for classified map breaks <- c(0, 0.90, 1)             # 0-90% = other areas, 90-100% = top 10% labels <- c("other areas", "top 10%")  # Plot the classified map with two colors top10_map <- priority_map(   baseline_folder,   classify = TRUE,   breaks = breaks,   labels = labels ) +   scale_fill_manual(values = c("lightgray", "darkgreen")) +   ggtitle("Priority map") +   theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),         legend.position = "bottom") +    labs(fill = "rank")  # Combine map and feature curves p1_combined <- top10_map + p5  print(p1_combined)

title: Exploring Zonation outputs
text: addition maps performance curves, can also explore coverage distribution selected priority fraction using function coverage_distribution(). histogram shows, coverage level (coverage bin) x-axis, number species reaching coverage level (y-axis). example, bar reaching 30 y-axis coverage range 0.1-0.2 means 30 species 10% 20% range included selected priority fraction.  overview Zonation results can created combining maps outputs.
code: p6 <- coverage_distribution(baseline_folder, target_rank = 0.9) +   ggtitle("Coverage at the top 10%") +   theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))  print(p6) p2_combined <- top10_map + p5 / p6  print(p2_combined)

title: Exploring Zonation outputs
text: looking combined visualization, can see areas top-priority (map), well species represented areas (feature curves), number species different coverage levels (histogram). provides full view spatial priorities feature-level coverage, illustrating ZonationR allows users explore interpret conservation outcomes flexible straightforward way.

title: Plot summary performance curves — summary_curves
code: # \donttest{ withr::with_tempdir({    data_path <- system.file(     "extdata",     package = "ZonationR"   )    dir.create("output")    file.copy(     file.path(data_path, "summary_curves.csv"),     "output/summary_curves.csv",     overwrite = TRUE   )    p1 <- summary_curves(     dir = ".",     output_folder_name = "output",     metrics = c("mean", "max")   )    print(p1)  })  # }
